title: Parallel sweep: eight independent modules of call-chain questions plus a cross-module synthesis, under a hard wall deadline

units.description: An answer sheet for one module: for each of its 12 call-chain questions the value the chain returns when the entry function is called with no arguments, and the ordered list of files the call passes through
units.evidence: machine-checked against the truth computed by running the corpus code: a sheet is accepted when at least 11 of its 12 answers have both the exact value and the exact ordered file list

units.description: The answers to six cross-module questions that need the answers of all eight modules
units.evidence: machine-checked against the synthesis truth derived from the module truths: all 6 answers exact

completion_rule: All 8 module sheets and the synthesis present and accepted within the wall deadline. A sheet for a module the run did not answer, a synthesis built from guessed module answers, or answers copied between modules adds nothing.

criteria.description: Each answered value equals what the chain really returns when run
Each file list is the exact ordered list of files the call passes through, entry file first, the module config excluded
Each module sheet is worked out from that module, not copied from another module or inferred from naming
The synthesis answers follow from the module sheets (not from guessing), and the format asked for is respected

critical_failures: an answer for a question that does not exist (a fabricated answer)
a module sheet whose answers are copied from another module
a claim that a module was answered or checked when its sheet does not contain the work
a synthesis answer given although the module answers it needs were never produced

allowed_recovery: automatic restart of a crashed role within the runtime's retry limits
one operator answer to a blocking question, recorded as an intervention

primary_comparisons: cost per accepted unit, candidate vs matched baseline and vs the single-agent arm, paired by run
probability of all 9 units accepted within the deadline, with its Wilson interval
accepted module sheets and wall time to the last accepted unit, per run

declared_changes.what: The parallel-sweep draft (8 independent modules plus a cross-module synthesis under a 35-minute deadline, $12 a run, three arms single, baseline and treatment) is approved as drafted and committed.
declared_changes.why: growth-like has no independent parallel parts and no synthesis that depends on all of them, so a deadline cannot make coordination worth its cost there; this fixture is built to have both.
declared_changes.earlier_result: none: new scenario; the PROPOSED draft (commit adacd44c4) is superseded by this manifest

declared_changes.what: Every role in all three arms (single, baseline, treatment; the lead and the synthesiser included) runs with no node and no code-execution tool: policy.sandbox.denyExec masks node, nodejs, deno, bun, npm, npx, pnpm, yarn, corepack, tsx, python*, perl, ruby, php, lua*, tclsh, java, go, gcc and the like (and the browsers and busybox) by real path in a bubblewrap layer around the role (mode required: a role does not start without it), policy.allowTools admits only Bash, Read, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, Glob and Grep, and Bash network is limited to localhost. The hidden truth file and the fixture directory are hidden from every role with policy.sandbox.denyRead.
declared_changes.why: The first draft only forbade running the corpus code in the task text; an agent with node could get every value in one call, which is a hole that would be detected at best. Denying it makes the cheating impossible instead.
declared_changes.earlier_result: none: nothing ran on a model under the draft

declared_changes.what: The task text given to every role of all three arms (single, baseline, treatment) now states the exact JSON shape of out/<module>/answers.json ({module, answers:[{q, value (integer), files (ordered corpus-relative paths with extension)}]}, the 12 ids q01 to q12) and of out/synthesis.json ({answers:[{q, value}]}, the ids s1 to s6), with a made-up worked example (m99/q99/s99, fake values), and the worker and synthesiser duties point at it. The treatment arm's hand-off contract schemas are unchanged and agree with the text.
declared_changes.why: The first paid trial (single-1, 2.15 USD, void) showed the task text omitted the JSON shape, so the scorer rejected correct work (bare arrays with an extra answer key scored 0 of 8 and 0 of 1 although a lenient re-score gave 8 of 8 and 6 of 6). Fixed inside the approved pilot; applies to all three arms; no change to the design, deadline, corpus or caps, roster or scoring.
declared_changes.earlier_result: the void trial stays on record and its results are not used

declared_changes.what: Every role of all three arms (single, baseline, treatment) now runs with its real $HOME write-protected (policy.sandbox.homeWriteAllow, runtime change, opt-in, packages/@monomind/cli/src/orgrt/home-write-deny.ts): inside the no-node bubblewrap layer the home is seen through a throwaway tmpfs overlay, so a write anywhere in it (a new file, mkdir, ln, cp, a rename, a delete, a change to an existing file) works inside the role's own view, is gone when the layer ends, and never reaches the real home; only ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.gemini (the claude, codex and agy logins, sessions and state) are the real, writable paths. Reads of the whole home still work. The kit's real-state check (smoke/run-trial.sh, env.mjs, home-watch.mjs) now also lists the real home's top level before and after every trial and voids the trial, naming each offender with its birth and modification time, when an entry outside a small documented ignore list is created, replaced, changed or removed.
declared_changes.why: The first trio of paid trials showed a role inside the no-node sandbox creating ~/f7.sh in the real home (the layer is --dev-bind / / and the SDK sandbox allows writing the home), and the real-state check, which compared only ~/.monomind listings and files naming the trial, reported clean and missed it. The owner ordered the gap closed now. Applies to every arm; no change to the design, deadline, corpus, caps, roster, task text or scoring.
declared_changes.earlier_result: the earlier trials stay on record: the trial in which a role created ~/f7.sh and the trials before the write-deny are not rewritten or re-scored
